desc: MemoHoney price, worked out per day: one capsule is one day, so each pack has a clean daily cost. Shipping, which pack fits your goal, and no subscription.
h1_b: What Each Package Costs Per Day
subhead: One capsule covers one day, which makes MemoHoney one of the easiest supplements in the aisle to price honestly. Here's the math for every pack, shipping included.
alt: Close-up of coins, illustrating the MemoHoney price per serving
takeaways: One capsule is one day. A bottle holds 30 capsules, so every bottle is exactly a month and the daily cost is the bottle price divided by 30.
Published prices at the time of writing: $79 a bottle in the 2-pack, $69 in the 3-pack and $49 in the 6-pack. Check the official page for today's number.
Shipping changes the small pack most. The 2-bottle order adds $9.99, which lifts its real daily cost from about $2.63 to about $2.80. The 3- and 6-packs ship free in the US.
There's no subscription. Each package is a one-time charge, so nothing renews unless you reorder.
The cheapest daily rate isn't always the cheapest decision. The 6-pack locks in six months before you know whether the formula suits you.
pull: A bottle is a month and a capsule is a day. Once you see the price that way, the packages stop being confusing.
body: The MemoHoney price, at the rates published when we wrote this, runs from about $2.80 a day on the 2-bottle pack (with its $9.99 shipping) down to about $1.63 a day on the 6-bottle pack, which ships free in the US. Each bottle is 30 once-daily capsules, so one bottle is one month.

Those numbers come straight from the package prices in our full MemoHoney review, where we also go through the label ingredient by ingredient. This page does one job: it turns each package into a daily and monthly cost, adds shipping where it applies, and helps you pick the pack that matches what you're actually trying to test.
How much does MemoHoney cost per bottle?

The seller lists three packages. There's no single-bottle option on the published price list, so the smallest order is two bottles. Prices go stale, and the manufacturer can change them without notice, so treat the figures below as a snapshot and confirm on the official order page before you pay.
Seen per bottle, the gap between the smallest and largest pack is $30 a month. That's the whole story of the discount: the more months you commit to up front, the less each month costs.
What does MemoHoney cost per day?

This is where the once-daily format pays off for the buyer. Plenty of memory formulas ask for two or three capsules a day, which means a "30-day" bottle can quietly become a 15-day bottle if you misread the serving. MemoHoney's serving is one capsule. Thirty capsules, thirty days. No hidden multiplier.
So the daily cost is simple division. Take the order total, add shipping if there is any, and divide by the number of days the order covers.

Notice the first two rows. Most price comparisons quote the 2-pack at $2.63 a day, which is correct for the product alone. Once the shipping line lands at checkout, the real figure is closer to $2.80. It's a small difference per day. Across two months it's ten dollars, and it's the reason the 3-pack ends up only about $39 more than the 2-pack while giving you a whole extra month.
Is the 3-bottle or 6-bottle pack the better deal?
On price per day, the 6-pack wins clearly. On risk, it's less obvious. Here are a few realistic buying paths over six months, using the published prices:

If you already know you'll take it for half a year, the 6-pack saves $120 against two 3-packs. That's real money. The catch is that you're paying for months four, five and six before you've seen what months one to three do for you.

Our view is the same one we gave in the review: for most first-time buyers, three bottles is the sensible starting point, and a reorder is the cheaper mistake to make. Paying a bit more per bottle to keep the option of stopping is a reasonable trade.
Which MemoHoney pack fits which goal?
The formula has two halves that work on different clocks, and that should drive your choice more than the discount does.

You're mainly curious about the blood-flow side. The arginine and citrulline ingredients act within hours or not at all. Two bottles is enough time to know, though the review's honest caveat applies: at these amounts, most people shouldn't expect to feel them.

You want a fair test of the botanicals. Ginkgo and bacopa are cumulative, and their research runs 8 to 12 weeks. Three bottles is the realistic floor, because two bottles ends right as the assessment window opens.
You've already used it and want to keep going. This is where the 6-pack makes sense. You're no longer gambling on fit, so the lower daily rate is pure saving.

You're buying for two people. Six bottles split between two adults is three months each at the lowest per-bottle price. Just remember the refund terms apply to the order as a whole, so check the official terms before you split one.

If you aren't sure which half of the formula you care about, our article on what ginkgo biloba does and doesn't do for memory is a useful read before you choose, since ginkgo is the ingredient most of the circulation story rests on.
What does a fair 12-week trial of MemoHoney cost?

Daily cost is useful, but the number most buyers should care about is the price of a proper test. The botanical half of the formula needs 8 to 12 weeks before research would expect any change, so a fair trial is about three months of uninterrupted use.

At the published prices, that's $207 on a single 3-bottle order. Trying to do it on the 2-pack doesn't work cleanly: two bottles run out at day 60, and topping up with a second 2-pack brings the spend to about $336 for four months, a good deal of it on a month you may not want. Stretching the capsules by skipping days doesn't save money either. It just turns a 12-week test into a half-dose test that answers nothing.
So when you budget, think in quarters. Roughly $207 buys one honest answer. If the answer is yes, the 6-pack brings later quarters down to about $147 each.
Only on the smallest pack, according to the published price list. The 2-bottle order carries a $9.99 shipping charge. The 3-bottle and 6-bottle orders ship free within the United States.

If you're outside the US, don't assume either figure applies. International shipping, duties and delivery times aren't covered by the prices we've seen, so read the checkout total carefully before you confirm. The number that matters is the last one on the page, not the one on the package card.
No. Each package is a one-time charge with no auto-ship attached, which is one of the things we flagged in the product's favor in the review. You order, you're billed once, and nothing renews.

That's worth knowing because the supplement world is full of "trial" offers that turn into monthly charges buried in the fine print. If a page selling MemoHoney ever presents you with a free trial, a recurring billing box or a monthly plan, you're probably not on the official order page. Close it and go back to the source.
Hand using a calculator next to a laptop, working out MemoHoney cost per day
One capsule a day makes the math simple: the bottle price divided by 30. At the 6-bottle price that's about $1.63.
How do you check the current MemoHoney price?

Prices in this category move. The manufacturer can change them, run a different offer, or adjust shipping, and any page quoting dollar figures (including this one) can fall behind. Here's how to get the real number in a couple of minutes:
Go to the official order page rather than a reseller or a search ad for a marketplace listing. MemoHoney is sold direct.
Check the domain in your address bar before you type any payment details.
Read the order summary, not the package card. The summary shows shipping and any tax, which is the total you'll actually pay.
Divide by days. Total paid divided by (bottles × 30). That gives you a per-day figure you can compare with anything else.
Look for the one-time charge wording and keep the confirmation email. You'll want it if you ever use the guarantee.
How does the price compare with other memory supplements?
At about $1.63 to $2.80 a day, MemoHoney sits in the normal range for a branded daily memory formula. It isn't a bargain-bin product, and it isn't priced like a luxury one either.

The fair comparison is the one we made in the review. If cerebral blood flow is the reason you're interested, a standalone ginkgo supplement gives you that one mechanism at a disclosed, research-level dose for less money. What MemoHoney adds for the extra cost is the amino acid side, the antioxidants, bacopa, and the convenience of one capsule that covers it all. Whether that bundle is worth the difference depends on how much you value simplicity.

Comparing it against products with very different formulas is harder. Our ranking of the best memory supplements of 2026 lines them up on cost per day alongside dose disclosure and guarantee, which is a more useful frame than sticker price alone.
How does the refund affect what you really pay?

The 60-day guarantee lowers your risk, but it doesn't make the purchase free to undo. Per the terms covered in the review, you request a refund by email, return all bottles (including empties), and pay the return shipping yourself. Some versions of the terms also ask for at least 30 days of use first.

Two price consequences follow. First, return postage on six bottles costs more than on two, so a larger order carries a slightly larger exit cost. Second, the window is 60 days from purchase, while the botanicals need 8 to 12 weeks. If you might want your money back, you'll have to decide around week seven. Build that into the pack you choose: if a refund is a real possibility, a smaller order keeps the exit cheaper. The review walks through those refund terms line by line.
Is there a MemoHoney coupon code?

The published pricing doesn't involve a coupon. The discount is built into the packages: $79, $69 or $49 a bottle depending on how many you buy. We'd be cautious with third-party coupon sites promising extra percentages off. At best they send you to the same page you'd have found yourself. At worst they lead somewhere that isn't the official store, which is a bigger problem than paying list price.
What you're paying for, and what you aren't

The price buys a once-daily, stimulant-free capsule with 12 ingredients, seven of them with a printed dose, made in the US in an FDA-registered facility that follows GMP standards. That last point describes the factory, not the product: facility registration isn't FDA approval.

It doesn't buy a proven result. No published trial has tested the finished formula, and evidence for an ingredient isn't evidence for a product. Ginkgo, bacopa, astaxanthin, blueberry and honey are on the label without amounts, so you can't check them against the research doses. The review explains why the single-capsule format limits how much of each can fit. Nothing here treats or prevents any disease, and if your memory has changed noticeably, a doctor's visit should come before any purchase. Our guide to memory loss versus normal aging covers where that line sits.
So which MemoHoney price should you pay?

If it's your first order, the 3-bottle pack at $2.30 a day is the one we'd point most people to. It's long enough to give the botanicals a real chance, it ships free, and it doesn't commit you to half a year of something untested.

If you've already finished a round and want to continue, the 6-bottle pack at roughly $1.63 a day is the clear value pick. The 2-bottle pack makes sense mainly if you only want to try the circulation side, or if keeping the refund cheap matters more to you than the daily rate.
Whichever you choose, confirm the price on the official page, take the free 3-minute memory test before your first capsule, and put the 60-day date in your calendar.
faq: How many capsules are in a bottle of MemoHoney?
Each bottle contains 30 capsules. The serving is one capsule a day, so one bottle lasts exactly one month. That makes the daily cost easy to work out: divide the bottle price by 30.
Can I buy just one bottle of MemoHoney?

The published price list starts at two bottles. The three packages are 2, 3 and 6 bottles. If a single-bottle option appears on the official page later, the per-day math is the same: divide the total, including shipping, by 30.
Will I be charged again after my first order?

Not according to the published terms. Each package is a one-time charge with no auto-ship subscription. Nothing renews unless you place a new order. If a checkout page shows a recurring plan or a free trial, you're likely not on the official store.
The package prices we've seen don't mention tax. Depending on where you live, tax may be added at checkout. Always read the final order summary, which shows the total you'll actually be charged.
Is MemoHoney cheaper than a standalone ginkgo supplement?

Usually not. A plain ginkgo product tends to cost less and gives you a disclosed, research-level dose of that one ingredient. MemoHoney costs more because it bundles ginkgo with bacopa, amino acids and antioxidants in one capsule, though the botanical doses aren't printed on the label.
Does buying the 6-bottle pack change the guarantee?

The guarantee is 60 days from purchase on every package. It doesn't stretch to cover six months of use. A larger order also means more bottles to return at your own shipping cost if you ask for a refund, so confirm the current terms before ordering.
Why do some sites show different MemoHoney prices?
Prices change, and pages written at different times show different snapshots. Some sites also aren't the official store. The reliable figure is the one on the official order page on the day you buy.
final_p: Prices change. See the current packages on the official site, work out your cost per day, and keep your 60-day date in mind.
